item.title: All hospital libraries directed to keep 3 books on Ziaur Rahman and Khaleda Zia
item.description:
The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has instructed all public and private hospitals and medical colleges across the country to procure and preserve three books on BNP (BAngladesh Nationalist Party) founder and former president Ziaur Rahman and former prime minister Khaleda Zia in their libraries.

A letter issuing the directive was sent by the Health Services Division of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare on 27 September.

The letter, signed by Senior Assistant Secretary of the Health Services Division Khandakar Rabiul Islam, stated that one set of three books published by Jatiyatabadi Prokashona must be purchased and kept in the libraries.

The books are “President Zia: Rajnoitik Jiboni” and “Begum Khaleda Zia: Jibon O Songram” and “Sobar Agey Bangladesh”.

Heads of various departments and directorates under the health ministry were instructed to take necessary steps in this regard.

The directive was forwarded for implementation to relevant offices, including the Medical Education and Family Welfare Division, the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), the Directorate General of Family Planning (DGFP), the Directorate General of Drug Administration (DGDA), the Directorate General of Nursing and Midwifery (DGNM), and the Directorate General of Medical Education (DGME).

Copies of the letter were also sent to the National Institute of Population Research and Training (NIPORT), the Health Economics Unit (HEU), the Health Engineering Department (HED), and the National Electro-Medical Equipment Maintenance Workshop & Training Center (NEMEMW & TC).

item.title: PM greets Hindu community on Durga Puja
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman today extended greetings to the Hindu community in Bangladesh and across the world on the occasion of Sharadiya Durga Puja, one of the major religious festivals of the Hindu community.

In a message today, he said that, according to Hindu beliefs, Goddess Durga comes to earth from heaven for the welfare of the world, ensuring the well-being of her devotees, destroying evil forces and nurturing creation.

“The destruction of evil forces and the worship of truth and beauty have given a unique significance to Sharadiya Durga Puja,” he said.

The Prime Minister said people of different faiths, groups and communities in the country would observe their respective religious festivals with great enthusiasm.

He said the celebration of religious festivals reflected the beauty of Bangladesh's age-old religious and social values and cultural traditions.

He said friendship, harmony, goodwill and fraternity among people of different religions, groups and communities as Bangladeshis were manifested through religious, cultural and social activities.

Tarique Rahman said, “Equality, human dignity and social justice are fundamental to all religions, while the welfare of humanity is one of their principal teachings.”

“Therefore, alongside practising their respective religious beliefs and cultures, it is essential for everyone to maintain an atmosphere of peace in society through mutual respect, honour and compassion among people,” he said.

Referring to the country's political transition, the Prime Minister said Bangladesh had once again embarked on the path to democracy following the ouster of fascist rule at the cost of thousands of lives.

He said a massive undertaking to rebuild the country had begun, adding that the government's commitment was to establish a welfare-oriented, safe and humane Bangladesh for all citizens, irrespective of political opinions, religion or ethnicity.

“May our diverse society and outlook on life be enriched by the message of harmony and amity. Religion belongs to individuals, while the state belongs to all. Everyone has the right to security, regardless of religion,” he said.

Addressing members of the Hindu community, the Prime Minister urged them to celebrate the festival across the country with enthusiasm, joy and confidence, without fear and in safety.

He extended his greetings to the Hindu community once again on the occasion of Sharadiya Durga Puja.

item.title: Durga Puja holidays: Banks, stock markets to remain open on Saturday
item.description:
Government offices and banks will remain open for regular operations tomorrow, Saturday, despite it being a weekly holiday, with stock market trading also taking place to adjust the holidays for Durga Puja.

All scheduled banks in the country will remain closed for three days, from 20 to 22 October, on the occasion of Sharadiya Durga Puja. The following two days, Friday and Saturday, are weekly holidays. As a result, banks will remain closed for five consecutive days, from 20 to 24 October.

Bangladesh Bank issued a circular last Sunday, instructing banks to remain open on 17 October (Saturday), despite it being a weekly holiday, and operate as on a regular working day.

The Ministry of Public Administration issued a notification on the Puja holidays on 7 October. According to the government holiday calendar, 20 October, Tuesday, had already been declared a holiday by executive order on the occasion of Maha Navami. The following day, 21 October, Wednesday, is a public holiday for Bijoya Dashami. A holiday was also declared by executive order on 22 October, Thursday, making 20 to 22 October a three-day holiday for Durga Puja.

Meanwhile, 23 and 24 October, Friday and Saturday, are weekly holidays. As a result, government employees will enjoy five consecutive days off from 20 to 24 October. However, government offices will remain open next Saturday (17 October), a weekly holiday, in lieu of the holiday on 22 October.

item.title: ‘Feed the children and put them to sleep, I’ll be a little late’
item.description:
“Feed the children and put them to sleep. I’ll be a little late getting home; I’m busy working on a news story.” Journalist Lutfuzzaman Alif Fakir had said this to his wife, Anondita Sangma, before leaving home.

Who could have known that this would be his last conversation with her? His wife had finished dinner and was waiting with their two children when she heard the news of her husband’s death. Lutfuzzaman had been shot dead by assailants.

At around 7:45 pm on Thursday, Lutfuzzaman, 44, left home after placing his one-and-a-half-year-old son, Aiyan Safayan, in his wife’s arms. A short while later he was shot dead in front of a village shop.

Anondita was devastated by the loss of her husband. Holding her son in her arms and sitting beside her husband’s body, she told Prothom Alo through tears, “I never imagined that someone could shoot a person dead within such a short time.”

Journalist shot dead in Netrokona

“When I was feeding the children, I heard the gunshots and initially thought someone was setting off firecrackers. A little while later, people started saying that he [Lutfuzzaman] had been killed,” she said.

Demanding justice for her husband, Anondita said, “I will never get my husband back. But I want the police to identify those who killed him and left my two young children without a father, and bring them to justice. I want them to receive exemplary punishment.”

Lutfuzzaman was shot dead in the Telonjia area of Durgapur upazila in Netrokona at around 8:15 pm on Thursday. He worked as the Netrokona correspondent for the private IPTV channel Ruposhi Bangla. He also ran a Facebook page called ‘Detective Article’, where he published articles and videos about various irregularities and crimes.

He was the son of Mohabbat Ali Fakir of Sunai village in Pogla union of Kalmakanda upazila. He lived at his father-in-law’s house in Telonjia.

Visiting the scene at around 10:00 pm, the tea stall where this happened was found on the veranda of a house beside a village road. The area was quiet. The house of Lutfuzzaman’s in-laws was about 20 yards from the shop. Inside, relatives were weeping.

Most residents of Telonjia village belong to the Garo community.

Lutfuzzaman’s paternal aunts-in-law, Nirala Rema and Ruli Rema, said they had been sitting and chatting on the veranda when they suddenly heard a loud noise. They rushed towards the shop and found Lutfuzzaman lying motionless on the ground. Blood was flowing from his head, neck and chest.

According to family members, Lutfuzzaman married Anondita Sagma, daughter of Shila Sagma and the late Philip Rangsa of Telanjia village, about six years ago.

Lutfuzzaman’s wife, Anondita Sagma, said they have two children: a four-year-old daughter, Pranti, and a one-and-a-half-year-old son, Aiyan Safayan.

The scene was visited by Netrokona Superintendent of Police Md Tarikul Islam, Additional Superintendent of Police (Crime) Mahfuza Khatun, Additional Superintendent of Police (DSB) Hafizul Islam, Durgapur police station Officer-in-Charge Khandakar Shaker Ahmed Khan, Durgapur Upazila Nirbahi Officer Ahmed Sadat, and other police and administrative officials.

According to eyewitnesses and police, Lutfuzzaman had tea at a roadside tea stall in the Telanjia area at around 8:00 pm. After finishing his tea, he set off for Birishiri Utrail Bazar. Realising that he had left his mobile phone at the stall, he returned about three minutes later.

As he was leaving with his phone, two young men arrived at the stall and asked the shopkeeper for cigarettes. They then fired several shots at Lutfuzzaman in quick succession. Hearing the gunshots, local residents rushed to the scene, and the two men fled on foot. Lutfuzzaman was rescued and taken to the upazila health complex, where a physician declared him dead.

Robin Rangsa, the tea seller in Telanjia, told Prothom Alo, “I was washing tea cups at the time. Lutfuzzaman had left his mobile phone behind, so he came back. As he was leaving with his phone, two young men came in and asked me for cigarettes. Then they shot Lutfuzzaman. I heard four gunshots in succession. I was frightened and went inside my house.”

According to Robin Rangsa, the two men appeared to be between 30 and 35 years old. One was wearing a lungi and the other three-quarter-length trousers. They fled when local residents came out after the shooting. He said the shots were fired from close range.

Speaking to journalists at the scene, Superintendent of Police Md Tarikul Islam said the initial assessment was that the killing had been planned beforehand. Several police units were working to arrest those involved, he said. Police recovered pistol cartridge cases and one unexploded round from the scene.

Police said all police stations in the district had been alerted following the killing, and checkpoints had been set up at various locations. CCTV footage from nearby areas was being collected and reviewed.

Earlier, on 10 November last year, assailants had hacked and injured Lutfuzzaman near the Teribazar ferry terminal on the Someshwari River in Durgapur upazila. When a colleague accompanying him tried to intervene, the assailants chased him while brandishing weapons.

Following Thursday night’s fatal shooting, Lutfuzzaman’s body was sent to the morgue at Netrokona Sadar Hospital for an autopsy.

item.title: Giant plastic monster with a tree in hand emerges on Cox’s Bazar beach
item.description:
A giant monster-shaped sculpture stands on the sand dunes of the Cox's Bazar sea beach. It has been made entirely from discarded plastic bottles. Tourists have gathered to see it. Some are taking photographs, while others are recording videos.

This was the scene at Sugandha Point on Cox’s Bazar beach last Wednesday afternoon. Bidyanondo Foundation has taken this unusual initiative to raise awareness about plastic pollution.

The organisation runs a ‘Plastic Exchange Store’ in Cox’s Bazar throughout the year. There, people can exchange discarded plastic for essential commodities, including rice, flour, sugar and edible oil. A portion of the plastic collected through this programme has been used to create the ‘Plastic Monster’ sculpture.

Cox’s Bazar Deputy Commissioner Md A Mannan inaugurated the sculpture exhibition on Monday, 12 October. Police Superintendent Sajedur Rahman and other officials were present at the event.

The sculpture will remain on display at the beach for the next four months. Films on tourism awareness will also be screened. Visitors will have to bring two discarded plastic bottles as an entry fee to watch the films.

The organisers said the ‘Plastic Monster’ sculpture was created to highlight how plastic used by tourists and local residents is polluting the sea and the harmful consequences of such pollution.

Through the four-month exhibition, they aim to raise awareness among several hundred thousand tourists and local residents about the harmful effects of marine pollution. The organisers said they want to encourage people to act responsibly in managing plastic waste.

Bidyanondo Foundation director Jamal Uddin said, “We often enjoy the beauty of the sea but forget our own role in polluting it. This monster, made from discarded plastic, is actually a reflection of our lack of awareness.

“We want people not just to take photographs of the sculpture and leave, but also to ask themselves where they are disposing of the plastic they use and what harm it is causing to the sea,” he added.

On the sculpture, Deputy Commissioner Md A Mannan said the sea is an important part of Bangladesh’s natural resources, biodiversity and economy. However, due to people's lack of awareness, plastic waste is threatening the marine and beach environment.

Such initiatives will bring the severity of pollution to people's attention and encourage changes in their behaviour. Everyone, including tourists, local residents, business owners and other stakeholders, must play a responsible role alongside the administration in keeping Cox’s Bazar clean, he added.

item.title: Indian police detain CJP founder Dipke ahead of protest
item.description:
INDIA-POLITICS-PROTEST

Police detained India's 'cockroach' movement founder Abhijeet Dipke on Friday, live images from his group showed, ahead of a protest called by him in capital Delhi's central business district, the latest rally to demand the resignation of India's election chief.

The youth-led 'Cockroach Janta Party' (CJP), opposition groups, and student organisations have held almost daily protests this month demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over a revision of voter lists that critics say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

More than 130 million voters were deleted during the revision but the Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol. The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.

Dipke called Friday's protest in support of two CJP leaders detained and sent to jail this week for five days for demonstrating at a protest site in violation of a ban.

The group and left-wing student organisations had urged supporters to gather at the Central Park in New Delhi's busy Connaught Place shopping and food district on Friday evening to wave and hoist the national flag.

The live video on CJP's Instagram handle showed Dipke coming out of a house and walking towards the street, where police officers stopped him and, after a brief argument, hauled him into a police car and drove away.

"We are detaining you right now," a police officer could be heard telling Dipke. "I have not broken any law right now...how can you detain me," Dipke asked the police officers as he was taken away.

There was no immediate comment from the police on the detention. Earlier on Friday, police met Dipke and warned him against going ahead with the protest.

item.title: Food on the plate, but is it nutritious and safe?
item.description:
On a morning in Sutrapur, Dhaka, Sabbir, a university student living in a shared mess, walks from one Grocery shop to another with a shopping bag in his hand. He checks the prices of rice, lentils and cooking oil before turning towards the vegetable stalls. At the fish market, he pauses, weighs the prices against his limited budget and eventually moves on to the egg seller.

His shopping list is longer than what his wallet can afford. He decides to leave some items behind and buy smaller quantities of others. By the time he returns to his mess, he has managed to buy food for the day—but not everything he had planned.

For Sabbir and countless families across Bangladesh, buying food has increasingly become an exercise in compromise. Some cut back on fish and meat; others skip fruits or choose cheaper alternatives. Even after bringing food home, another concern remains: is it safe to eat?

The struggle is no longer simply about putting food on the table. It is about whether people can afford nutritious meals and whether the food they consume is safe.

Observed on 16 October every year, World Food Day marks the founding of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO). Since 1981, the day has highlighted the global fight against hunger and the need to ensure food security for all. In Bangladesh, however, a fundamental question remains: when food is available, why do so many people still struggle to access adequate, nutritious and safe meals?

More food, yet persistent insecurity

Bangladesh has made considerable progress in agricultural production. Yet increased output does not automatically translate into food security for every household. Food may be available in markets, but families without sufficient purchasing power cannot necessarily afford it.

Floods, excessive rainfall, crop losses, unstable employment and inflation further complicate the situation, particularly for vulnerable communities whose livelihoods depend on daily wages or agriculture.

According to the FAO's Global Information and Early Warning System (GIEWS) Bangladesh Country Brief, published on 4 September, 2026, approximately 18.1 million people in Bangladesh could face acute food insecurity between September and December 2026, compared with an estimated 15.3 million during May–August. High inflation, declining purchasing power and flood-related livelihood losses were identified as contributing factors.

The figures underline an important distinction: food security is not simply about producing enough food nationally. It also depends on whether people can obtain that food when they need it.

When a day labourer's income falls, the family's meals may become smaller or less diverse. A low-income household might manage to buy rice but struggle to afford fish, eggs, milk or fruit regularly. Farmers who lose crops to natural disasters may also find themselves unable to purchase sufficient food.

The challenge, therefore, lies in addressing poverty and insecure livelihoods alongside agricultural production.

Rising prices, shrinking diets

For low-income families, rising food prices can quickly turn everyday shopping into a difficult balancing act. A large share of household income already goes towards food. When the prices of rice, lentils, cooking oil and vegetables increase, families may have little choice but to reduce spending elsewhere—or compromise on what they eat.

A Prothom Alo report citing a World Food Programme (WFP) survey found that 24 per cent of the population surveyed experienced food insecurity. Among the ultra-poor, the figure was 46 per cent. The report also noted that 71 per cent of surveyed households identified rising food prices as a major concern. These figures reflect the survey period and should not be interpreted as current prevalence rates.

The consequences extend beyond household budgets. Fruits, milk and animal-source foods are often among the first items families reduce or eliminate. Fruits such as oranges have also become increasingly difficult for some consumers to afford. For families with children, providing a varied and nutritious diet becomes an even greater challenge.

Rice and potatoes can help satisfy hunger, but they cannot, on their own, meet all nutritional requirements. The body needs proteins, vitamins, minerals and other essential nutrients for healthy growth and functioning.

Food security must therefore be measured not only by the availability of staple grains but also by the affordability of fish, eggs, milk, pulses, vegetables and fruits.

Children bear the nutritional burden

Among the most troubling consequences of food insecurity is inadequate nutrition during early childhood. The first few years of life are critical for physical growth, brain development and the development of the immune system. Insufficient dietary diversity during this period can have lasting consequences.

A UNICEF report published on 6 June, 2024, titled Child Food Poverty: Nutrition Deprivation in Early Childhood, estimated that nearly two-thirds of children under five in Bangladesh—approximately 10 million—experienced child food poverty. The report found that these children did not receive the minimum dietary diversity recommended for adequate nutrition. Approximately one in five faced severe child food poverty, consuming food from only one or two food groups.

Child food poverty is not simply a matter of eating too little. It also reflects the absence of essential nutrients and variety. A child may feel full after eating rice, yet still lack adequate nutrition if the diet regularly excludes eggs, fish, pulses, milk, vegetables and fruits.

UNICEF's preliminary findings from the 2025 Bangladesh Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS) paint a similarly concerning picture. Only 35 per cent of children aged 6–23 months received minimum dietary diversity, while just 30 per cent received a minimum acceptable diet.

These findings point to a challenge that cannot be solved through awareness alone. Families also need the financial means to purchase nutritious food. Maternal health, access to healthcare, safe water, sanitation and appropriate childcare all influence children's nutritional outcomes.

Making nutritious foods affordable, strengthening maternal and child nutrition programmes, and expanding school-based nutrition initiatives are therefore essential steps towards improving children's well-being.

When food itself becomes a health risk

Affordability is only one side of food security. The other is safety.

Food purchased from a market may satisfy hunger, but contamination or adulteration can turn an everyday meal into a potential health risk. Harmful chemicals, unauthorised ingredients, unsafe dyes and contamination caused by unhygienic production or storage can all compromise food safety.

A Daily Star report published on 3 February, 2026, citing data from the Bangladesh Food Safety Authority, found that 571 of 1,713 food samples tested during the 2024–25 fiscal year had irregularities involving adulteration, contamination or nutritional standards. This represented approximately 33.3 per cent of the samples examined.

The tested products included pickles, sauces, chips, puffed rice, fruit drinks, mustard oil, butter, soybean oil and honey.

These findings do not mean that one-third of all food products in Bangladesh are unsafe; they relate specifically to the samples tested during that fiscal year. Nevertheless, they highlight the importance of stronger monitoring and consistent quality control.

Food safety must be maintained at every stage, from production and processing to transportation, storage and sale. Regular inspections, stronger laboratory capacity, transparent publication of test results and effective action against violations are essential. Consumers must also have accessible ways to report suspected adulteration and seek accountability.

For families already struggling to afford food, unsafe products create an additional burden: they must worry not only about whether they can buy enough food, but also about whether what they buy will harm their health.

Beyond hunger: A shared responsibility

Ensuring food security in Bangladesh requires a coordinated approach that connects agricultural production with affordability, nutrition and food safety.

Low-income households need better access to fairly priced essential foods and effective social safety-net programmes. Farmers need affordable production inputs, adequate fertiliser supplies, fair prices for their produce and support when natural disasters destroy their livelihoods. Better storage, transportation and supply-chain management can also help reduce waste and improve access to food.

At the same time, stronger food safety enforcement and targeted nutrition programmes are necessary to protect consumers, particularly young children and other vulnerable groups.

World Food Day serves as a reminder that food security cannot be judged solely by how much a country produces. The more important questions are whether families can afford adequate meals, whether children receive the nutrients they need and whether the food reaching consumers is safe.

Bangladesh's progress in agricultural production is significant, but the challenge remains far from resolved. Rising prices can push nutritious food beyond the reach of low-income households, children can suffer from inadequate dietary diversity, and food safety violations can undermine public health.

Building a hunger-free Bangladesh requires more than filling stomachs. It demands a food system in which nutritious meals are affordable, safe and accessible to everyone—not a privilege reserved for those who can afford them.

Sources: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), UNICEF, Prothom Alo, WFP, The Daily Star.

item.title: ‘Beef Feast’ in protest against notice, cow bought for Tk 125,000
item.description:
In protest against an administrative notice asking students to refrain from slaughtering animals on campus, a group of students at Jagannath University (JnU) slaughtered a cow and organised a feast on campus on Friday.

The cow was slaughtered on the road between the Vice-Chancellor's residence and the Mathematics Department as part of a pre-announced programme titled "JnU Students' Beef Feast".

According to the organisers, beef and khichuri will be distributed among students after midday.

Earlier, a controversy sparked over cooking beef khichuri near the Muktamancha on the campus. Following this, the university administration issued a notice advising against animal slaughter on campus. This drew outrage from some students.

Protesting the move, the Jagannath University Central Students' Union (JnUCSU) held demonstrations and rallies, eventually announcing the programme to slaughter a cow and hold a feast on Friday.

Notably, most members of JnUCSU's elected committee, including the Vice President (VP) and General Secretary (GS), are leaders of Islami Chhatra Shibir, student wing of Jamaat-e-Islami.

Cow costs Tk 125,000

On Thursday, a cow was bought for Tk 125,000 for the feast. JnUCSU Assistant General Secretary (AGS) Masud Rana invited everyone to join the programme, adding that the cow was bought using student registration fees alongside donations from various individuals at home and abroad.

When the cow was brought to the campus on Thursday evening, organisers took out a celebratory procession, chanting slogans defending their right to consume beef and protesting the administration's decision.

Some students framed the initiative as a direct protest against the administration’s earlier notice.

When contacted, JnU Proctor (additional charge) Professor Azam Khan said, "We had issued the city corporation's notice regarding cattle slaughter in the form of a notification to maintain law and order. We will have no objection if the feast is organised in a proper and disciplined manner with the administration’s permission."

How the controversy started

On the night of 12 October, students of the 2021–22 academic session from the Department of Islamic History and Culture arranged a beef khichuri feast near the Muktamancha on the campus to celebrate completing their undergraduate studies. The university's central temple is situated near that spot.

Several Hindu students raised objections to the cooking arrangement, alleging that preparing beef in front of the temple hurt their religious sentiments.

Allegations were also raised that bricks from the temple were used to build the makeshift cooking stove. Hindu students staged protests on campus over the incident.

However, the student organisers stated that their initial plan was to cook inside the university cafeteria. Due to low gas pressure, they opted for an earthen stove using firewood as an alternative. Upon learning that the bricks belonged to the temple, they removed them and brought iron stoves from the cafeteria. They also expressed regret for the unintentional mistake.

The university administration stated that the issue was resolved immediately through the proctor’s intervention, with further discussions held between the relevant parties the following day. However, after the incident surfaced on social media, it triggered intense debates and counter-allegations.

Notice advising against animal slaughter

On 14 October, the university proctor's office issued a notice instructing everyone to refrain from slaughtering animals on the campus, citing the protection of public health, cleanliness and the maintenance of a hygienic environment. It warned that violating the instructions would invite action in line with Dhaka South City Corporation's public notice.

Following the notice, several students alleged that by issuing directives against animal slaughter, the administration had infringed upon their dietary choices and rights to cultural practices.

In protest against the notice, JnUCSU brought out a protest procession and held a rally on campus on Wednesday night. From the rally, they placed a four-point demands, including the withdrawal of the notice, a public apology, an investigation into the incident, the inclusion of beef and mutton in the cafeteria menu, and ensuring religious harmony on campus.

The JnUCSU leaders gave the administration a 24-hour ultimatum to issue an apology. They announced plans to slaughter a cow and hold a feast on Friday, setting a registration fee of Tk 70 for participating students.

Administration clarifies notice, expresses regret

Following criticism over the notice, the university administration clarified its position. In a statement issued through the Public Relations, Information and Publication Office, the JnU administration said everyone has the right to organise any event on campus, including animal slaughter.

However, all must remain mindful that no event causes disruption to the programmes or activities of others.

The statement added that the proctor had requested restraint regarding animal slaughter to prevent unwarranted tension and avoid deterioration of communal harmony in light of recent developments.

The administration expressed regret for the misunderstanding caused by the request.

Despite the administration’s explanation, JnUCSU proceeded with its announced "beef feast" programme.

item.title: Saudi Arabia executes two Bangladeshi for indecent acts inside Mecca mosque
item.description:
Saudi Arabia has executed a Bangladeshi man and woman after they were convicted of committing indecent acts inside a mosque in the holy city of Mecca, Saudi Interior Ministry announced, reports Gulf News.

The ministry identified the two as Nazrul Islam Abdul Basir and Siti Akhtar, both Bangladeshi nationals, according to a statement carried by the Saudi Press Agency (SPA).

The statement said security authorities arrested the pair after they committed what it described as immoral acts inside a mosque in Mecca, reports the news outlet.

Following an investigation, the two were charged and referred to a competent court, which found them guilty and sentenced them to death under ta'zir, a discretionary punishment under Islamic law.

The ministry said the court imposed the sentences because of the seriousness of the offence and the violation of the sanctity of the mosque and the circumstances in which the acts were committed.

The verdicts became final after being upheld by the relevant judicial authority, and a royal order was issued authorising their implementation. The executions were carried out on Wednesday, 14 October 2026, in the Mecca region.

In its statement, Saudi Interior Ministry reaffirmed the Saudi government's commitment to maintaining security, upholding justice and enforcing Islamic law against those who violate the sanctity of mosques.

It also warned that anyone committing similar offences would face punishment under the kingdom's laws, reports Gulf News.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,186 as five die in 24 hours
item.description:
Five more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Friday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,186.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all five of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,082, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 104, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the five new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in Chittagong, with two deaths reported in both the Chittagong division and Chittagong district.
A total of 1,164 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Friday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 211,040.
During the same period, 46 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 22,972.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 187,615 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 180,002 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: BGB: No compromise on border security
item.description:
The Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) will not make compromises on any issue related to border security, including illegal entry and attempts to push people across the border, a senior official said on Friday.
Between January 1 and Thursday this year, the force foiled 182 push-in attempts across 23 districts, stopping 1,275 illegal entries, said Lt Col Md Mahbub Murshed Rahman, director (operations) of the BGB, at a press conference at the BGB headquarters.
He said the BGB is performing its duties with vigilance, restraint and professionalism to prevent attempts to forcibly push in people across the border.
The force has intensified surveillance and maintained communication and coordination with relevant stakeholders to prevent such incidents, Mahbub added.
He said the BGB is strictly following existing laws, regulations and established protocols in dealing with illegal activities along the border.
It is also increasingly using modern surveillance equipment, day-and-night observation technology and other advanced tools to strengthen border security, the official said.
Alongside its security operations, the BGB continues to support border communities through medical services, skills development for young people and various welfare initiatives, he said.
The BGB has also intensified operations against illegal arms, narcotics and other contraband items.
During various drives this year, the force recovered around 78 pistols, seven rifles, one submachine gun, seven grenades, 12 landmines and more than 3,200 rounds of ammunition.
It also detained 1,957 people suspected of involvement in smuggling narcotics, weapons and other contraband and handed them over to the respective police stations for legal action.
According to BGB data, the force seized smuggled goods worth around Tk 2,086 crore between January 1 and October 15. The seized goods included narcotics, gold, textiles and cosmetics.
The operations are aimed at protecting the country's economic interests and ensuring legitimate trade, the BGB official said.
The BGB has seized more than 26 million Yaba tablets since January this year, along with around 40 kg of crystal methamphetamine, 12 kg of heroin and cocaine, nearly 16,000 kg of cannabis, about 24,000 bottles of Phensedyl and around 1 lakh bottles of foreign liquor.
The force considers preventing drug trafficking a top priority, as narcotics pose a serious threat to young people, families and public security.
BGB members are working round the clock to prevent drug trafficking and smuggling, Mahbub said

item.title: DNC seizes 244 liters of liquor and beer in Gulshan raid
item.description:
The Department of Narcotics Control (DNC) has seized 244 liters of foreign liquor and beer during a raid on a rest house in Gulshan of the capital and arrested its manager.
The arrestee is Md Ataur Rahman Shamim, 42, manager of 78 Rest House Society on Road 104 in Gulshan-2.
The DNC also named Md Omar Jamil, 45, who is linked to the establishment, as a suspect. He is currently absconding.
A case was filed with Gulshan Police Station against Shamim, Jamil and other unidentified individuals.
Acting on intelligence that the establishment had been storing and selling foreign liquor and beer without a valid bar license, a DNC team conducted the raid around 2:30am on Friday, said Md Mehedi Hasan, deputy director of the DNC’s Dhaka Divisional Intelligence Office.
The seized items included 223 bottles of foreign liquor containing 177 liters and 209 bottles and cans of beer containing 67 liters.
The DNC said the establishment also operated under the name “German Club”.
Preliminary investigations found no evidence of a legitimate or authorized entity operating under that name.
According to the DNC, the premises hosted DJ parties where tickets were sold, and foreign liquor, beer and other narcotics were allegedly supplied illegally to participants.
Mehedi said investigations are underway to trace the absconding suspect and establish the nature of the activities conducted under the name of German Club.
The DNC said the drive is part of its ongoing efforts to curb the illegal storage, sale and distribution of narcotics and other controlled substances.

item.title: BSF returns two Bangladesh police personnel detained in India
item.description:
India’s Border Security Force (BSF) returned 2 Bangladesh police personnel nearly 15 hours after they were detained by Indian citizens after crossing into Indian territory through the Brahmanpara border in Comilla.
They were handed over at around 1:30pm on Friday following a battalion commander-level flag meeting between the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) and BSF at the Shashidal border in Brahmanpara upazila, according to a BGB press release.
The 2 released personnel are Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) Imran Hossain and Constable Rohit Dewan of Brahmanpara police station. Officer-in-Charge (OC) Faruk Hossain of the police station confirmed the matter.
Commanding Officer of Sultanpur Battalion (60 Battalion) Lt Col SM Shariful Islam, Shashidal Border Outpost Commander Subedar Mohammad Takbir Hossain, Assistant Superintendent of Police (Debidwar Circle) Md Shahin and Brahmanpara Police Station OC Md Faruk Hossain attended the meeting.
According to police sources, a police team went to an area near border pillar No 2059 in Ashabari, Shashidal union, Brahmanpara upazila, at around 10:30pm on Thursday, October 15, to conduct a drug recovery operation.
While chasing a suspected drug trader, Constable Rohit Dewan unknowingly crossed the border and entered Indian territory. Several Indian residents subsequently detained him and handed him over to the BSF.
When ASI Imran Hossain attempted to secure his colleague’s release, he was also detained. Police and senior BGB officials then began contacting Indian authorities to secure the return of the 2 personnel.
Earlier, at a press conference at the BGB headquarters in Pilkhana, Dhaka, at 11:30am on Friday, Lieutenant Colonel Md Mahbub Murshed Rahman, director of the BGB, said formal communication had taken place with the BSF.
He also said the 2 police personnel were unharmed.

item.title: Two arrested over mob killing in Satkhira, prime accused at large
item.description:
A murder case has been filed over the lyincing of Wahiduzzaman Shamim, a man with mental health issues, in Debhata, Satkhira, following allegations of religious insult and incitement through Facebook Live and posts.
Shamim’s elder brother, Abdul Jalil, filed the case with Debhata police station on Thursday night, naming 10 people, with Fazlul Haque Ameni of Parulia named as the prime accused. Another 200-250 unidentified people have also been accused.
Police have arrested two people in connection with the case, including Moktar Hossain and Asadul Molla.
According to the case statement and family members, Shamim became involved in a domestic dispute with his wife on Monday evening and allegedly used abusive language. A local person later circulated an audio recording of the exchange on social media.
Claiming that the recording contained derogatory remarks, local resident Fazlul Haque Ameni went live on Facebook and called on the people to attack Shamim.
A mob subsequently attacked the family’s home and vandalised property.
Shamim was also assaulted near Subarnabad market, according to his elder brother, Abdul Jalil.
Following the attack, Shamim returned home and consumed poison, his family said.
He was taken to the chamber of a local physician, MA Sabur, in the Kuliya area, where he received treatment and was kept under observation.
On Tuesday, a mob entered the doctor’s chamber and attacked him again. Police intervened, rescued Shamim and took him to Sakhipur Health Complex.
However, the violence did not end there.
According to the family, another large mob entered the health facility, assaulted Shamim and dragged him outside.
Jalil alleged that Ameni led the crowd, which he estimated numbered more than 1,000 people.
The attackers allegedly slammed Shamim against a wall and beat him severely.
Police subsequently recovered him and transferred him to Satkhira Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared him dead.
OC Shahin confirmed that Shamim had been attacked again after police initially rescued him.
“At 8:30pm, an agitated mob, or ‘Tawhidi Janata’, whatever one might call them, arrived and assaulted him again,” he said.
Shamim’s family described the killing as deliberate and demanded action against those responsible for mobilising the crowd.
“They incited people against him using a provocative video/audio clip, and then deliberately and systematically beat him to death,” Sagar said.
Sagar said his brother had completed his Honours and Master’s degrees in History at Jagannath University.
According to the family, Shamim developed mental health problems after being drugged by criminals during a bus journey several years ago.
He had experienced periods of mental instability for around a decade and had been receiving medical treatment.
The family said his condition had affected his personal life, including his first marriage.
Shamim leaves behind two sons, one from each marriage.
Sagar questioned why his brother had been subjected to mob violence instead of being dealt with through the legal system.
“If the law had punished him, we would have accepted it. But why should my brother be beaten to death without any trial?” he said.
The victim’s family also alleged that local Jamaat-e-Islami activists were involved in mobilising people during the initial attack.
Sagar claimed that some participants had gathered at a local Jamaat office before proceeding to the family’s home.
He alleged that local party leaders and activists were among those involved.
However, Kamrul Islam Gazi, president of the Ward 8 Jamaat-e-Islami unit in Parulia Union, denied the allegations.
He told BBC Bangla that local residents, rather than Jamaat activists, had assaulted Shamim.
“No... it was the local residents,” he said when asked whether party members were involved.
Gazi said he had heard that Shamim was beaten after being taken for treatment following his consumption of poison.
The family’s allegations against Jamaat members have not been independently established.
As of 3pm on Thursday, no murder case had been filed, according to police.
OC Shahin said police had contacted the victim’s family and were expecting them to visit the police station to lodge a complaint.
Sagar also said the family intended to file a case later in the day.
Police said the investigation was continuing and that legal action would be taken against those identified as responsible.

item.title: Two women killed in road accident in Shyamoli
item.description:
Two women were killed after being hit by a speeding vehicle while crossing the road in the capital’s Shyamoli area early Friday.
One of the victims was identified as Mukta, 40, while the identity of the other woman, estimated to be around 45, has yet to be confirmed.
Both were reportedly residents of the area.
The accident occurred beneath the overbridge near Shyamoli intersection early on Friday.
Police said a speeding vehicle struck the two women as they were crossing the road and fled the scene. One woman died on the spot.
Mohammadpur police rushed to the scene and rescued Mukta in an injured condition before taking her to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, where she died while undergoing treatment.
The bodies have been kept in the hospital morgue for autopsies.
Mohammadpur police station Officer-in-Charge Abdul Halim said police had identified one of the victims but were still trying to establish the other woman’s identity.
He added that police were also working to identify the vehicle involved in the accident.

item.title: Italian teenager Cisse nets hat-trick as AC Milan run riot in Salzburg
item.description:
AC Milan secured their first win of the 2026/27 Europa League campaign in emphatic fashion, thrashing Salzburg 4-0 at the Red Bull Arena thanks to a stunning hat-trick from Italian teenager Alphadjo Cisse and a goal from Gonçalo Ramos.
The Rossoneri responded in style to their opening defeat against Benfica, with Cisse stealing the spotlight in a record-breaking performance.
The teenager became the youngest Italian player to score a hat-trick in a European club competition match, underlining his growing potential on the continental stage.
Club-record signing Ramos added Milan’s fourth goal in the 72nd minute, capping an impressive attacking display.
However, Filippo Terracciano’s red card took some of the shine off the victory for Ruben Amorim’s side.

item.title: Yamal on song
item.description:
There is much debate over who should win the Ballon d'Or this year, but if Lamine Yamal's recent form continues over the season, handing out next year's award would be simple.
The teenage winger was at his mesmerising best as Barcelona waltzed to a 4-1 win at Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday, to make it 10 victories from 10 matches this season across all competitions.
Hansi Flick's irresistible side have scored 43 goals in that spell, including seven in the last two games, even without talisman Raphinha.
A sensational dribble from Yamal helped create a goal for Anthony Gordon in Istanbul, and the winger's inviting cross also carved out another for Fermin Lopez.
"I don't know what to call it, it was an almost-rabona dribble," Yamal told Movistar.
"It came off well to set up Gordon, that's the main thing, that it was effective at the end of the day."
Yamal had a moment of luck when the ball bounced off the defender back to him but showed excellent reflexes and speed to keep it in and find the former Newcastle winger.
The 19-year-old was named player of the match and earned lavish praise from his coach after another performance in which his ability to beat defenders and generate danger proved decisive.
"It's amazing to have a player like him on this level. He changed the game for us and this was really good," Barca coach Flick told reporters.
"In the second half he was fantastic, how he dominated the game, the (final ball)... it's unbelievable what he's doing."
Yamal has eight goals and nine assists in 10 games for Barcelona this season.

item.title: Infantino offers apology but 'no answers' at FIFA meeting over World Cup plan
item.description:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino gave "no satisfactory answers" when grilled Thursday during a meeting to discuss his attempts to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors, senior members of football's global governing body said, but he did offer an apology for the failed project.
"We asked a great many critical questions, but there were no satisfactory answers from my point of view," said Bernd Neuendorf, the head of the German Football Association (DFB), who is also a member of the FIFA Council.
Neuendorf was speaking after the Council met behind closed doors at the body's Zurich headquarters, where Infantino's FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal was one of the main topics on the agenda.
Infantino has been under severe pressure since his announcement in late July that he wanted to open FIFA's premium competitions such as the World Cup to private investors.
That plan was ultimately abandoned in the face of widespread criticism, with a rebellion led by European governing body UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and CONCACAF, which runs the sport in North and Central America and the Caribbean.
"I apologised for the mistakes that we made in relation to the communication and consultation process related to the FIFA Forward Enterprise project," Infantino said in a video published by FIFA.
"But what is important to remember is that it was a proposal, so in no way a done deal, just a proposal, that actually intended to enable FIFA to invest more in our member associations."
However, the FIFA chief reaffirmed that the FFE initiative "has been permanently withdrawn and will not reappear in any form".
Infantino has headed FIFA since 2016 and is running for re-election next March, despite calls for him to stand down in the wake of the FFE plan.
For the moment, no heavyweight candidate has put themselves forward to run against him.
Debbie Hewitt, the chair of the English Football Association who is also a FIFA vice-president, told reporters that Infantino is "not fit to be FIFA president" unless he releases all documents pertaining to the failed sell-off plan and answers key questions.
Hewitt and Neuendorf are among the 36 members of the FIFA Council, along with Infantino.
"We were asked to submit our questions" in relation to the plan which was not put to the FIFA Council before the July announcement, Hewitt said.
"One of the disappointing things was we didn't get answers. We didn't get answers to anything we had specifically requested, for example getting the papers from FFE, and so we asked the question why and why not."
Many leading European national associations have withdrawn their support for Infantino in the upcoming election because of the uproar caused by FFE and other controversies, including his relationship with US president Donald Trump.
Chief among those were Infantino's decision to create a FIFA Peace Prize and award it to Trump at last December's World Cup draw, and the decision to suspend a ban for United States striker Folarin Balogun following a red card during the World Cup after Trump intervened directly by phoning Infantino.
"I speak for myself as a Council member -- from my position nothing has shifted," Hewitt added. "I have no new information that makes me feel any differently to how I felt when I went in, other than we do have a president of FIFA who is apologetic about what has happened, and secondly a promise again that we will get the information that we have requested."
FIFA confirmed its intention to set up a $6.35-billion development fund for the next four years, a plan which is expected to be finalised by the Council at its next meeting in December.
To finance the fund, which would allow money to be distributed to FIFA's 211 federations as well as to the regional confederations, it would draw in part on its financial reserves after a commercially successful 2026 World Cup.
The plan would allow for the payment of $25 million to all 211 member federations.
Infantino may hope the latest plan reinforces his position ahead of the election.
The deadline for submitting candidacies is November 18.

item.title: Lyon down Palace in Europa League, Sunderland leave it late
item.description:
French club Lyon held off Crystal Palace 3-2 in the Europa League on Thursday, while Sunderland made a late comeback to break the hearts of Portuguese second-division side Torreense.
Bayer Leverkusen, Juventus, Benfica and Bournemouth all also won to maintain their perfect starts to the league phase.
It was a painful return to his old home for Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage as the UEFA Conference League champions fell to their fourth defeat of the season in all competitions.
"It's a very disappointing return because we lost. I can't take satisfaction from coming back home or seeing familiar faces when the result isn't there," Sage told UEFA.com.
"The scoreline may have been close, but there was a big difference in the way the two teams played. We were nowhere near our usual standards in the first half."
Lyon took the lead inside the opening 10 minutes through Corentin Tolisso and Ernest Nuamah then doubled Lyon's advantage two minutes into first-half injury time.
Yeremy Pino halved the deficit for Palace early in the second period, but a close-range flick by Pavel Sulc restored Lyon's two-goal buffer.
Daichi Kamada smashed home a second for Palace with nine minutes remaining but the hosts held out to make it two wins from two to start the league phase.
Bayer Leverkusen followed up their opening 2-0 win with a 4-0 success at Polish side Lech Poznan.
AC Milan cruised to a 4-0 victory at Red Bull Salzburg, courtesy of a hat-trick scored by Italian teenager Alphadjo Cisse.
Club-record signing Goncalo Ramos made it four on 72 minutes before a red card for Filippo Terracciano took some of the sheen off the win for Ruben Amorim's men.
In the Estadio Municipal de Leiria, Portuguese Cup winners Torreense looked set to hold their Premier League opponents to a draw until Noah Sadiki's 93rd-minute strike made it 2-1 for the visitors.
The 15th-placed side in Portugal's second tier stunned Sunderland in the 37th minute as centre-half Volnei Feltes cut past a flimsy challenge and unleashed a piledriver 30 yards from goal, which left Robin Roefs rooted to the spot.
Black Cats boss Regis Le Bris sent on first-team regulars Granit Xhaka and Enzo Le Fee just shy of the hour and the move paid dividends as Jules Ahoka struck shortly afterwards to level the scores.
After a lengthy VAR check decided against awarding Sunderland a late penalty, Torreense must have thought they had done enough to earn a famous point until Sadiki popped up at the death to thrash in the winner.
"Conceding a goal in the last minute is a blow to the chest," Torreense coach Carlos Simoes said. "The players are in the dressing room, devastated."
Fellow Premier League outfit Bournemouth enjoyed a fine home debut in Europe as they eased to a 3-0 win over Sturm Graz, courtesy of goals by Evanilson, Rayan and Alvaro Rodriguez.
Juventus fought from behind to emerge 2-1 victors at Celta Vigo after Newcastle loanee Nick Woltemade made it two from two in Europe to cancel out Hugo Alvarez's opener for the hosts, and Randal Kolo Muani scored an injury-time winner.
Martin O'Neill's Celtic continued their difficult start to the season as they sank to a fourth defeat in their last five outings, outclassed 4-1 at Benfica.
